title: Ye te sahasram: the thousand nooses of Death
theme: Death’s thousand, ten thousand nooses, set to kill the mortal, are all to be removed by the power of the sacrifice.

words.role: dative of the one aimed at
words.context: The anonymous commentator reads it as an accusative by interchange: every living being
The anonymous commentator: «हन्तवे हन्तुं» — to kill

words.meaning: by the power, by the art
words.context: The anonymous commentator gives two readings: «मिषेण च्छद्मना» (by the means, the device) and «मायाशब्दः शक्तिपर्यायः» (māyā means power)

words.meaning: we remove by sacrifice, we sacrifice away
words.context: The anonymous commentator: «तान्सर्वान्पाशानवयजामहे निवारयामः» — we ward off all those nooses

sandhi.type: final m before a vowel; final m before a consonant; visarga after ā before a voiced consonant
sandhi.rule: sahasram is joined to ayutam; ayutam becomes ayutaṃ before p; pāśāḥ before m drops its visarga.

morphology.note: A Vedic infinitive in -tave from √han: ‘to kill’, glossed by the commentator with the classical infinitive hantum.

√yaj with ava means not ‘worship’ but ‘remove by sacrifice’, ‘sacrifice away’; the commentator says so: «अत्रोपसर्गयोगेण यजतेर्भिन्नार्थतोच्यते» — joined to the prefix, yaj is said to have a different sense.
The base prints a comma after tān (तान्,), marking a pause in recitation; it does not change the words.

translation.literal: Which nooses of yours, O Death, a thousand, ten thousand, [are there] to kill the mortal — all those we remove by the power of the sacrifice.
translation.readable: Death, your nooses for killing mortals number a thousand, ten thousand: by the power of the sacrifice we take them all away.

anvaya: हे मृत्यो ते ये सहस्रम् अयुतम् पाशाः मर्त्याय हन्तवे [सन्ति] तान् सर्वान् यज्ञस्य मायया अवयजामहे ।
syntax: A relative clause (ye … pāśāḥ) with numbers in apposition and a dative of purpose with an infinitive (martyāya hantave), resumed by tān … sarvān as object of the main verb avayajāmahe, with the instrumental yajñasya māyayā.

ambiguities.note: The commentator gives both senses: the sacrifice as a device or pretext, «मिषेण च्छद्मना», and the sacrifice’s power, «मायाशब्दः शक्तिपर्यायः». The Vedic sense of māyā as wondrous power is the second; the first is his alternative.

metre.name: anuṣṭubh
metre.note: As printed 18 + 15 syllables: ye te sahasram ayutaṃ (8) pāśā mṛtyo martyāya hantave (10); tān yajñasya māyayā (7) sarvān avayajāmahe (8). The second pāda has ten and the third seven; the edition reports the counts.

beginner: This prayer is addressed to Death and pictures him as a hunter with snares: a thousand, even ten thousand nooses, all set to catch and kill mortal beings. The speakers say that by the power of the sacrifice they take all those nooses away. The verb used does not mean "worship" here; with its prefix it means "to remove by sacrifice", and the old commentator points this out. He gives two ways of hearing "by the power of the sacrifice": either by means of the sacrifice, or by its strength. In this Upaniṣad the verse comes just before the offerings made "to Death". The edition reports what the words and the commentator say; it makes no claim about what the rite achieves.
analogy: Like a trapper’s snares laid across a field, found one by one and lifted before anyone steps into them.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: It speaks to Death of his nooses, a thousand and ten thousand, set to kill the mortal, and says that by the power of the sacrifice the speakers remove them all.

commentary.q: How does the commentator read it?
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The anonymous commentator: «हे मृत्यो मर्त्याय व्यत्ययेन» — the dative ‘for the mortal’ stands by interchange for the accusative, so the nooses are there to kill every living being. ‘We remove them’ means we ward them off, «तान्सर्वान्पाशानवयजामहे निवारयामः», because joined to its prefix the verb yaj changes its sense, «अत्रोपसर्गयोगेण यजतेर्भिन्नार्थतोच्यते». The ‘māyā of the sacrifice’ is either the device of good works or their power: «मायाशब्दः शक्तिपर्यायः».

schools.disagreement: No Vedānta-school commentary on this anuvāka is in the edition’s sources (Raṅgarāmānuja’s commentary on the Mahānārāyaṇa is not among them). The anonymous bhāṣya explains the words and the rite; it does not argue an Advaita, Viśiṣṭādvaita or Dvaita position here, so the edition gives none.

contemporary.text: The image multiplies death’s snares beyond counting and answers them not with fear but with an act done deliberately and together. Facing an overwhelming threat by doing what can be done is an old human response. This is a modern reflection on the passage, not part of its traditional meaning.

reflect.beginner: What ‘snares’ — habits or dangers — would you most want removed from your path?
reflect.deeper: Why might the prayer count the nooses in the thousands and ten thousands rather than naming them?
reflect.practice: Identify one small ‘snare’ in your routine and remove it today.

references.text: No comment of Sāyaṇa’s or Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara’s on this anuvāka is in the edition’s sources: Sāyaṇa’s anuvākas 52–57 are missing from the digital text used here, and neither commentary file glosses these words; the edition’s concordance maps give no anuvāka of theirs for it. The anonymous bhāṣya is the only commentary quoted.

flags.note: The Tirupati e-text alone lacks तं in अयुतं (सहस्रमयु पाशा), a witness error (corrections.json).
